blocks.note: PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for good
Mary Quant, the 1960s designer credited with popularising the miniskirt

explanation.surface: A tribute to a fine designer of yesteryear whose work was exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is the crossword shorthand for pious, hence good; Mary Quant was the London designer of the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: A piquant flavour or remark is sharp and pleasantly exciting, so stimulating is a direct synonym.

blocks.note: surface reading: an electrical safety switch on a railway line
setter's reading: a halt that interrupts a car's laps of a motor-racing track

explanation.walkthrough: Circuit breaker sounds electrical, but the circuit is a lap of a racetrack and the breaker is the pause in the pit lane.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a car leaves the track briefly for fuel or tyres, interrupting its run of laps.

clue.text: District record broken by bit of a swimmer, a competitor as yet unbeaten?

indicators.note: something broken by an intruder is split open with the intruder sitting in the gap

blocks.note: a quarter is a district of a town
a list is a written record
a fin is part of a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local record is smashed by a swimmer who has not lost a race yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The record that is broken is the district and the list taken together, so the intruding pair lands at the join rather than inside the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who reaches the last eight of a knockout tournament has not been beaten so far, hence the question mark.

blocks.note: the letters of the alphabet that come before N to Z run from A to M

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A to M' as a single word: it is exactly the half of the alphabet preceding N-Z.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny particle or smallest possible piece of something, as in not an atom of truth.

clue.text: Training device still wobbling, on being secured

indicators.note: a wobbling object is unsteady and its parts shift out of place
one item is secured inside the other, held in its grip

blocks.note: taken as written
RE means on or about, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: A piece of exercise equipment is still shaking even after being fastened down.
explanation.walkthrough: Training is meant in the gardening sense: climbing plants are trained to grow along a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice frame guides climbing plants such as roses or vines in a chosen shape, which gardeners call training them.

clue.text: With sun going in, shoot bird

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A hunter waits for the sun to set before shooting a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoot looks like a verb about hunting; it is the noun for a sprouting bud.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bustard is a large heavy ground-dwelling game bird of open grassland.

clue.text: Noises made by animals importing meat in island country

indicators.note: something importing goods takes them inside its borders

blocks.note: baas are the bleats of sheep
ham is cured pork

explanation.surface: Livestock bleating as they are shipped with meat cargo into an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commonwealth of the Bahamas is an archipelago nation in the Atlantic, south-east of Florida.

blocks.note: first meaning: omit, pass over
second meaning: hop or bound lightly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one instruction about a missed leap, but the two parts are separate senses of a four-letter verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both leaving something out, as in skipping breakfast, and moving with light bounds.

clue.text: Long time to wait for June’s ice cream, might you say?

indicators.note: asks for the phrase as it would be spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: June is a month, and its ice cream treats would be its sundaes

explanation.surface: Someone wanting ice cream in June faces a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: A sundae is an ice-cream dessert; said aloud, a month's worth of them matches the idiom spelt with Sundays.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an extremely long period, used of something that will not happen for ages.

blocks.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
something that itched was irritating

explanation.surface: Losing a diamond ring turned out to be a real annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to discard or get rid of, so something ditched has been dumped, abandoned, cast off.

clue.text: Our hero in a state unfortunately, appear distraught

indicators.note: an unfortunate state of affairs suggests letters that have come to grief and landed in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Our protagonist is in a terrible way and looks utterly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' seems to describe the hero's mood but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes showing extreme anxiety or frustration, as though pulling at one's own head in despair.

clue.text: Repetition of cheers for so long

blocks.note: TA is British slang for thanks, given twice

explanation.surface: Raising glasses again and again as a farewell toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is meant as British thanks, and TA is the informal word for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual British ways of saying goodbye, informal farewells used when parting.

blocks.note: first meaning: as in ... for, decide on
second meaning: rather fat, rounded

explanation.walkthrough: Stout tempts one towards beer; here it is the adjective for a rounded figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb appears in plump for, meaning decide on, and the adjective describes a pleasantly rounded, chubby body.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their join

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A batsman's runs being pursued in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Score looks like runs in cricket; it means to scratch a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut marks into it, which is what engraving with acid or a point does.

blocks.note: TAB is a key on a computer keyboard
by means beside, close to

explanation.surface: A key left lying close to the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabby is a domestic feline with a striped or mottled coat.

blocks.note: first meaning: cheerful, festive
second meaning: slightly tipsy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'very drunk', but jolly is a separate sense, not an intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cheerful and lively, and in British use also mildly tipsy after a few drinks.

indicators.note: tells us which piece comes later in the word
something that jerks is jolted out of place, so its letters move

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sudden painful twinges after a workout, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerks reads as a noun; it is a verb acting on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs express uncertainty, meaning that something may or may not be the case.

clue.text: Builder of muscle in feeble editors

indicators.note: feeble suggests something weak that falls apart, letting its letters scatter

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Muscle-building drugs found among weak newspaper editors.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs of this class are used, often illicitly, by athletes to increase their bulk and strength.

clue.text: Colourful band in front introduced by artist

indicators.note: the introducer comes first, leading in what follows

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A painter presenting a vividly dressed group of musicians at the front of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians but is a stripe of colour; RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectral hues in the sky forms a curved strip of seven colours.

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other means it sits inside

blocks.note: red is a colour
to fuse is to blend together

explanation.surface: A mixing of colours that was rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss a request or offer is to turn it down, decline, reject it outright.

clue.text: Thingummy with a hollow shaft, broken

indicators.note: a hollow thing has had its insides removed, so only its outside letters stay
something broken is in pieces that can be put together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A gadget whose hollow shaft has snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a' looks like linking words but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal placeholder words for an object whose proper name you cannot remember.

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: Peru's, the South American country with a possessive
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Examining a nation's frontiers when you arrive there.
explanation.walkthrough: Borders seems to belong to the country, but it acts on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, so the noun study is a synonym.

clue.text: Concern there’s pressure guaranteed when leader gone

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and it is gone

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
certain means guaranteed, sure

explanation.surface: Worries about a pledge being honoured once the boss has left.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that concern a subject relate or belong to it, which is what the verb pertain expresses.

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for very drunk
second meaning, cryptic: without a leg, a stage of a journey or race

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an actor too drunk to perform; a leg is a stage of a relay or journey.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for so drunk one cannot stand, and literally lacking a leg, which is a stage.

blocks.note: first meaning: a regiment's or ship's colours, its banner
second meaning: tire, lose energy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as dyes losing brightness, but colours is the plural noun for a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or regiment's colours is its banner, and a runner who flags is tiring and slowing.

indicators.note: something designed is newly planned and made, so letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A city in Iraq planned by Arab architects.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is the main port city of southern Iraq, on the Shatt al-Arab waterway.

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way

blocks.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: Arms wrapped around someone in a warm hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Arms suggests limbs in an embrace; it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosy and comfortably warm, as of a sheltered room or bed.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tad, a little bit, roughly quite

explanation.surface: Someone rather distressed by the details collected about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for analysis, the information gathered in research.

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is left off

blocks.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A stage play abandoned halfway, and filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot looks like a film or gun word; it is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of whisky or other spirit, just as a shot is.

clue.text: Dizzying flight from Paris, as articles flying all over the place

indicators.note: things flying all over the place end up scattered in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disorienting plane trip out of Paris, with luggage tossed everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight is not an aeroplane journey but a set of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps, and climbing a helical one round and round can make you giddy.

clue.text: Take away first of trunks, transported back

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter
back means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the initial letter
carted means carried, transported

explanation.surface: Removing the first of the trunks, which had been shipped back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to lessen its value, taking away from its worth.

clue.text: Just punishment is required after revolutionary observed stealing millions

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word is reversed
something stealing an item takes it in and holds it
says which piece comes last in the word

blocks.note: seen means observed
M is the abbreviation for million
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary caught pocketing millions deserves the retribution coming to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is required' looks like wordplay, but 'is' gives letters; it is the 'required after' that tells us order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, from the Greek goddess of retribution, means deserved downfall or retributive justice.
